questions.question:
34 is related to 191 by certain logic. Following the same logic, 56 is related to 301. To which of the following is 63 related, following the same logic?

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (1st number × 5) + 21 = 2nd number.

Now,

For, 34 : 191

⇒ (34 × 5) + 21 = 170 + 21 = 191.

For, 56 : 301

⇒ (56 × 5) + 21 = 280 + 21 = 301.

Similarly, for 63 ∶ ?

**⇒ (63 × 5) + 21 = 315 + 21 = 336.**

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All computers are printers.

Some printers are laptops.

All laptops are mobiles.

Conclusions:

I. Some printers are computers.

II. Some laptops are printers.

III. Some mobiles are laptops.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow.
Only conclusions I and III follow.

questions.solution:
**Statements:**

All computers are printers.

Some printers are laptops.

All laptops are mobiles.

The least possible Venn diagram:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2dbb1bf0082a2af2e666166abe1da35aba7e8f11ba581081db59ca91f85b7f80.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some printers are computers. - **True **(because All computers are printers so, Some printers are computers too)

II. Some laptops are printers. - True (because Some printers are laptops so, Some laptops are printers too)

III. Some mobiles are laptops. - True (because All laptops are mobiles so, Some mobiles are laptops too)

Hence, the correct answer is **"All the conclusions follow".**

questions.question:
Select the number that will come in the place of the question mark(?), if ‘+’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged

31 ÷ 3 – 186 × 6 + 17 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Given equation: 31 ÷ 3 – 186 × 6 + 17 = ?

Now, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged, then:

⇒ 31 × 3 + 186 ÷ 6 – 17 = ?

⇒ __**31 × 3**__ + 186 ÷ 6 – 17 = ?

⇒ **93** + __**186 ÷ 6**__ – 17 = ?

⇒ __**93 + 31**__ – 17 = ?

⇒ **124 – 17** = ?

⇒ __**107**__.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**.

questions.question: Each of the letters in the word 'LASTING' is arranged in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical series between the letter which is second from the left end and the one which is fourth from the right end in the new letter-cluster thus formed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2b15de16d396b52c68424915920e099dae05b94ac6a08cd00b03ee850fcc8e27.png] 

The logic followed here is:

Given word: 'LASTING'

Each of the letters in the word 'LASTING' is arranged in the English alphabetical order.

LASTING → A**G**I**L**NTS

The letter which is second from the left end = **G**

The one which is fourth from the right end = **L**

**Thus, Four **letters (G, __**H, I, J, K**__, L) are there in the English alphabetical series between the letter which is second from the left end and the one which is fourth from the right end in the new letter-cluster thus formed.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Four".**
